deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. The sheet is a reused printed Latin doctoral diploma from the Faculty of Law at Heidelberg. The right part is cut away.

The printed text can be restored along the usual formula: 'NOS DECANUS SENIOR C[ETERIQUE PROFESSORES] ORDINIS JURI[SCONSULTORUM] IN LITTERARUM UNIVER[SITATE RUPERTO-CAROLA] IN VIRUM DOCTISSIM[UM] HENRICUM [...] MOENO-FRA[NCOFURTANUM] EXAMINE RIGOROSO SUM[MA CUM LAUDE?] [SUPERATO] GRADUM [DOCTORIS ...] SUMMOS IN UTROQ[UE IURE HONORES] RITE CONTULIMUS ET HOC DIPLOMATE SIGIL[LO ORDINIS ... COMPROBAVIMUS]. P. P. HEIDELBERGAE IN UNIVERSIT[ATE ...] D. XIV MENSIS [...]'. Below this are a laurel-wreath vignette, a large initial 'L', and the printer's line 'TYPIS ...'.

In plain terms, it is the printed diploma conferring the doctorate in both laws (utriusque iuris) on a 'Henricus' from Frankfurt am Main. The name, year and month are cut off.

The faint pencil notes over the print are a draft of the editorial table of contents written out cleanly on the previous page (26r). That outline sorts Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments by page and leaf ('S.', 'Blatt') into three groups:
- I. Erkenntnistheoretisches: (1) Grundbegriffe der Mathematik und Physik; (2) Molecularmechanik; (3) Gravitation und Licht.
- II. Psychologisches.
- III. Naturphilosophie.

The page references in the pencil draft match the fair copy closely: S. 7–10, S. 1–3, S. 38–40 (Blatt 16 u. 17), S. 3–7 (Blatt 3 u. 4), S. 11–21/32–36, S. 24–26, S. 26–31, S. 45, S. 36–38 (Blatt 15), S. 40–44. This is posthumous editorial or archival bookkeeping, apparently in connection with the Nachlass edition (compare the note 'in Bd. 18 vollständig enthalten'). It is very probably not in Riemann's hand and is not a derivation.

There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Draft table of contents / ordering of Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments (epistemology, molecular mechanics, gravitation and light, psychology, natural philosophy), written on a reused Heidelberg law-doctorate diploma
results.usually_credited_to: Posthumous editors of Riemann's Nachlass (cf. Dedekind/Weber edition of the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts')

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only a printed diploma used as scrap paper and a faint pencil draft of an editorial table of contents, which duplicates the previous page. It has no mathematical or scientific content.
transcription_corrections: The printed lines can be completed per the standard formula: 'ORDINIS JURI[SCONSULTORUM]', 'IN LITTERARUM UNIVER[SITATE RUPERTO-CAROLA]', 'MŒNO-FRA[NCOFURTANUM]' (= of Frankfurt am Main), 'SUMMOS IN UTROQ[UE IURE HONORES]'. The diploma is therefore a law doctorate (doctor utriusque iuris).
The first pencil heading 'Gesetze[?] der Mechanik[?] und Physik[?] S. 1–10' should probably read 'Grundbegriffe der Mathematik und Physik S. 7–10', as in the fair copy on 26r.
'S. 2 – 36' is probably part of 'S. 11–21, 32–36' (Gravitation und Licht).
Under II, 'S. 4 – 16' should probably read 'S. 24–26', and 'S. 16 – 31 ... S. 45' should read 'S. 26–31 ... S. 45'.
The pencil notes are probably not in Riemann's hand. They are editorial.
